sections.name: Body Armor
sections.card:
Summary: A blue-vest pickup that pads your health against gunfire, explosions and fire; in San Andreas it is shown as a bar rather than as hit points.
Uses: Armor works as padding on top of your health, but in San Andreas it gives no protection from falls.
Where to get it: Ammu-Nation sells it for 200 once the mission Doberman is done, it also lies as a pickup in set places, and climbing into a police or SWAT Enforcer van gives you some.

sections.name: Health pickups
sections.card:
Summary: A spinning heart pickup that fills your health to its maximum; in San Andreas they turn up during gang wars and in most missions with a lot of gun fights.
Uses: Other ways to heal in San Andreas: eat food, step into an Ambulance for up to 20% or a Hotdog van for up to 40%, or save the game at a save point.
Tips: Your maximum health can be raised by paramedic side missions and by exercising: sprinting, swimming or going to a gym. If your health runs out you are wasted, taken to the nearest hospital, charged a fee and stripped of your weapons, and any mission in progress fails.

sections.name: Safehouses and save points
sections.card:
Summary: Outside a mission you save by collecting the floppy diskette pickup at an available safehouse; saving also restores your full health and skips six in-game hours. The Johnson House is the save point you start with.
Uses: Safehouses can have a garage for up to four vehicles, a wardrobe for the clothes you have bought, rewards for collectibles, and some pay a daily asset income.
Tips: To buy one, collect the green house pickup and press the Action button; a blue house pickup is not unlocked yet. If a car will not fit, park a car in the garage door's way so it cannot close, then park the one you want inside. All 37 save points are needed for 100% completion and cost $879,000 in total.

sections.name: Police bribes
sections.card:
Summary: A spinning star-shaped police badge pickup; each one you collect takes one star off your wanted level.
Uses: Other ways to lose a wanted level in San Andreas: change clothes at a safehouse or clothing shop, respray at a Pay 'n' Spray, modify a car at a Mod Garage, start the Freight Train Challenge or a vehicle school lesson, buy a plane ticket to another city, or finish a mission.
Tips: Bribes are scarce, so it helps to memorise where they lie; some sit at a slight height and need a jump in a vehicle. Higher-level police already chasing you, such as the military, SWAT or the FBI, keep coming after a bribe, though no new law enforcement vehicles appear. The exception is the Police Maverick, which gives up at three stars and drops you to two.

sections.name: Jetpack
sections.card:
Summary: A one-person jetpack that lies on the ground like a weapon pickup and switches on the moment you walk into it; it is dropped when you press the vehicle exit button.
Uses: It makes you invulnerable to falling, crashing into walls or moving vehicles, and landing on a moving helicopter. Only one-handed weapons work while you fly it: Pistol, Tec-9, Micro SMG and Sawn-off Shotgun.
Tips: After the mission Green Goo it waits at Verdant Meadows Airfield beside the asset collectible, and it is a great choice for collecting horseshoes around Las Venturas. It has a much lower altitude limit than aircraft and is not ideal for scaling taller buildings.

sections.name: Heat-Seeking Rocket Launcher
sections.card:
Summary: A shoulder-fired homing launcher. It picks the nearest target itself: the marker is green on a vehicle and turns red after 3 to 5 seconds, which means the missile is locked on.
Uses: It is useful for taking out air vehicles such as Police Mavericks, and the missile flies much faster at aircraft. It can destroy any vehicle instantly.
Tips: Fired with no target, the rocket explodes after 100 to 200 meters, and you cannot sprint, jump or crouch while holding it. It lies at Easter Bay Airport in San Fierro, at Mike Toreno's ranch after Vertical Bird, beside an abandoned house in Aldea Malvada, and on a parking lot roof near Pilson Intersection in Las Venturas.

sections.name: Wanted level one and two stars (police)
sections.card:
Summary: One star brings an officer on foot, one or two police cars and, in towns, HPV1000 motorbikes. Two stars brings three officers on foot and, on water, Predator boats.
Weak points: At one star only one officer at a time chases you, with a nightstick, and the police eventually lose interest and the star fades on its own, unless you are in a police vehicle.
Tips: From two stars officers shoot even if you are unarmed or holding a melee weapon, and police cars may appear at intersections to block you. Being busted fails any mission, strips your weapons and costs $100 at one star or $200 at two.

sections.name: Wanted level three and four stars (SWAT, Police Maverick)
sections.card:
Summary: At three stars a Police Maverick helicopter arrives and drops SWAT members armed with Micro SMGs, and police occasionally set up armed roadblocks. At four stars SWAT chase in Enforcer vans and a News Chopper joins the Maverick.
Danger: Four-star roadblocks are made of the heavier Enforcer vans, which are harder to ram through. Shooting down the News Chopper only gets it replaced by another Police Maverick, so two police helicopters chase you.
Tips: From three stars police motorcycles give way to cars and officers start to appear on the sidewalks when you are on foot. Entering a region or city you have not unlocked gives four stars at once. Being busted costs $400 at three stars or $600 at four.

sections.name: Wanted level five stars (FBI)
sections.card:
Summary: At five stars the FBI takes over most of the chase: eight officers on foot (regular, SWAT and FBI), three FBI Ranchers or police cars, Predator boats on water, one or two Police Mavericks, and two Hydra jets if you are in the air.
Weak points: Their Rancher roadblocks are relatively easier to ram through, but the agents can make short work of your vehicle and drive very aggressively, which makes it easy to crash and lose control.
Tips: The agents carry fast-firing SMGs. Entering or flying over Area 69 or Easter Basin Naval Station gives five stars at once, but the areas around them only give four stars before they are unlocked. Being busted costs $900.

sections.name: Wanted level six stars (army)
sections.card:
Summary: At six stars Military soldiers with M4s chase you in Barracks OL trucks and Rhino tanks, alongside officers, Predator boats on water, Police Mavericks, and three Hydra jets if you are in the air.
Danger: The soldiers have very high precision and fire rate, the tanks may try to crush you, and the roadblocks are Barracks OL trucks with troops, which are very hard to ram through. That makes it nearly impossible to survive for long on foot.
Weak points: The tanks only chase and never fire their cannons. A car that hits a tank is only set on fire, not blown up at once, which gives you a chance to get out and keep escaping.
Tips: Six stars is not handed out instantly without cheats, which makes it very hard to reach; the level opens up after Yay Ka-Boom-Boom and in practice can be reached after Learning to Fly. Being busted costs $1,500.
